item.title: Robert Pattinson 成为第七任 007
item.description: 英国演员 Robert Pattinson 成为继 Daniel Craig 之后的第七任 007，将出演首部由亚马逊制作的 007 电影。Robert Pattinson 也成为第一位出演过蝙蝠侠的 007 演员。在 Daniel Craig 获选饰演 007 时，他当时还不是一线明星；相比其他竞争第七任 007 的演员，Robert Pattinson 已经是一位知名度极高的明星，大多数人都听说过他的名字。亚马逊显然是希望由一名有强大票房号召力的明星领衔主演其首部 007 电影。

item.title: Poll shows that 35% of Trump voters skipped the midterms
item.description:
New survey results show that 35% of President Donald Trump's 2024 voters didn't cast a ballot in the midterm elections.

The findings suggest Republicans' crushing losses this month were driven largely by Trump supporters staying home rather than abandoning the GOP for Democrats, according to a new J.L. Partners analysis reported by the New York Post.

The pollster found that low Republican turnout accounted for 10 percentage points of the 15-point swing toward Democrats since 2024, while voters switching parties accounted for the remaining five points.

Just 8% of Trump's 2024 supporters voted for Democrats on Nov. 3.

"The GOP should not throw the MAGA baby out with the bathwater just yet," J.L. Partners founding director James Johnson said, the Post reported.

"If Republicans can energize their 2024 vote in 2028, then they may yet have a shot at winning again."

The analysis, based on an Election Day survey of 1,000 registered voters and more than 30,000 campaign interviews, found particularly steep turnout declines among key segments of Trump's coalition.

Among his 2024 supporters, 46% of those without college degrees failed to vote, along with 44% of those older than 65 and 39% of rural voters.

Johnson said the turnout collapse alone would have cost Republicans control of Congress, even without voters switching parties.

"Even without a single voter switching, the GOP would have lost the Senate and House," Johnson said.

The findings bolster Trump's argument that Republicans suffered because he wasn't on the ballot.

However, Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis suggested GOP voters stayed home because they were dissatisfied with congressional Republicans' performance.

"A lot of our voters who stayed home, they stayed home because they were frustrated with the lack of productivity from Republicans in the House and Senate," DeSantis told Fox News.

The survey also found potential vulnerabilities for Democrats heading into 2028.

Nearly half of Democrat voters, 48%, said their midterm vote was primarily against Trump rather than in support of Democrat policies.

Only 30% of registered voters believed Democrats have a viable presidential candidate for 2028.

Meanwhile, CNN reported that Trump's declining popularity remains a significant obstacle for Republicans.

CNN's voter polling found that 86% of Americans who disapproved of Trump's performance backed Democrats in House races.

Cost of living emerged as the leading concern across every demographic group in the J.L. Partners survey.

Johnson suggested the Iran war contributed to voter frustration over rising prices, particularly gasoline.

The survey's overall margin of error was 3.4 percentage points.

Despite the GOP's losses, Johnson said the results indicate Republicans could rebound by rebuilding turnout among Trump's 2024 supporters rather than abandoning the political coalition that returned him to the White House.

item.title: California sues OpenAI, alleging it endangered the public by building AI without safeguards
item.description:
California sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging it failed to rein in powerful, potentially dangerous artificial intelligence technology.

California Atty. Gen. Rob Bonta’s office said the San Francisco-based company behind ChatGPT “misled and endangered the public by knowingly developing and testing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect the public.”

Bonta’s office alleged that an AI attack in July — in which OpenAI models broke out of an offline space, connected to the internet and hacked into Hugging Face, a rival AI company — was “entirely foreseeable in light of OpenAI’s choice to test models it knew to be dangerous in a flawed and exploitable testing environment without proper oversight.”

OpenAI spokesman Drew Pusateri said in a statement to The Times that the lawsuit “appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab.”

He said the company has “undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity” since the Hugging Face incident, including by strengthening safeguards across its systems and creating a “framework for additional identification and disclosure” of unintended activity, and will “continue to engage” with Bonta’s office “to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.”

The company previously called the Hugging Face attack a “warning shot” and pledged to make investments to prevent similar incidents.

Bonta’s office said the company’s “disregard for the public safety” created a “public nuisance” in violation of a law prohibiting businesses from engaging in “unfair” or “fraudulent” practices.

“While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability,” Bonta said.

The lawsuit directly challenges a rapidly growing industry that has been a massive economic boon to the state. An August report found that in 2026, California attracted $366 billion in industry-related venture capital — about 90% of all venture capital in the U.S., and three times more than every other state combined.

The funding — half of it linked to just two companies, Anthropic and OpenAI — helped the state move from a multibillion-dollar fiscal deficit to a multibillion-dollar surplus, according to budget projections.

The lawsuit also follows a public reckoning in recent months over claims from industry insiders that AI technology is developing too rapidly and poses an existential threat to human society.

OpenAI has suggested in the past that one of the better ways to ensure AI is safe is to release it broadly. Chief Executive Sam Altman and Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki once wrote on their company’s website that its “first commitment is to build AI in service of humanity” and in a way that empowers “people broadly,” not just a concentrated few.

“We believe the safer future is one where power is broadly distributed, so more of the world can participate in building a resilience ecosystem,” they wrote. They went on to say that “AI resilience refers to the collective organizations, systems, and individuals that society could put in place to anticipate, withstand, adapt to, and rapidly recover from AI-driven disruptions.”

They compare building AI safeguards to making automobiles safer by improving road infrastructure and enforcing seat belt and traffic laws. “The goal wasn’t to stop people from driving — it was to make a powerful technology resilient enough for widespread use,” they wrote.

The company called the Hugging Face attack “evidence that, without proper safeguards, highly capable AI agents are now able to work around technical controls, collaborate through unapproved channels, and take dangerous actions that no human directed.”

Bonta announced a formal investigation into the Hugging Face attack and served the company with an investigative subpoena in September — part of a broader probe of mounting cybersecurity incidents involving OpenAI, Bonta’s office said. On Monday, his office said such attacks “may just be the tip of the iceberg,” but the scope of the problem isn’t fully known because OpenAI hasn’t answered “detailed questions” about them.

In its own review of the Hugging Face hack alongside third-party auditors, OpenAI found that more than 700 AI agents began coordinating with each other via thousands of messages to escape containment and begin the unsanctioned attack. Subsequent investigations revealed similar testing of unreleased AI models had resulted in other cyberattacks, including on Wikipedia and government websites — sparking fears that future hacks could undermine increasingly critical infrastructure.

Earlier this year, Trump signed a voluntary safety-standards accord with AI executives to establish AI protocols. California has gone further, passing more than two dozen AI-related bills, including measures that establish a state framework for independent AI safety auditors.

Separate from the case in California, OpenAI announced Monday that it will allow four independent third-party evaluators to monitor how its systems behave as they are tested ahead of public release.

“This access gives assessors the evidence and context to pursue independent evaluations and uncover failures we may not have anticipated,” OpenAI said in a statement.

Bonta said Monday that securing public safety will require litigation and legislation in all 50 states and at the federal and international levels — and that he refused to accept that society should “pass off the blame to machines” while letting those who create them escape accountability.

“The people who created, who create, and operate these machines need to accept the responsibility for their actions,” Bonta said at a news conference Monday.

“Whether it’s a car or a toy, the law is simple: Don’t build or test things that can hurt people without proper safeguards,” he said.

Bonta’s office said it is encouraging “anyone with information relevant to this case” to contact it at oag.ca.gov/report.

He said his office is also watching other AI companies “closely,” but declined to elaborate.

Sign up for Essential California for news, features and recommendations from the L.A. Times and beyond in your inbox six days a week.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times.

item.title: Ground stop chaos spurs fight in Congress over air traffic control funding
item.description:
WASHINGTON – Congress is under pressure to act after air traffic control issues grounded flights nationwide last week, setting up a new funding fight on Capitol Hill and further complicating lawmakers' efforts to avoid another government shutdown before Christmas.

Trump administration officials are pleading for billions of additional dollars to modernize what they acknowledge is an aging system. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said he's asking lawmakers to fast-track a $50 billion package to prevent further communications malfunctions like the one that derailed air travel before the weekend.

Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are already voicing skepticism about the request, with Democrats pointing to unused Federal Aviation Administration funds and Republicans balking at the topline number.

Despite those concerns, there's a near-universal understanding on Capitol Hill that the FAA's systems are in desperate need of a revamp. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Maryland, indicated on CNN over the weekend that while Congress has "given the administration what they asked for," there could be an openness to additional spending.

"If they need more, they should come up and justify it," he said. "I will support what is necessary to have a safe system and a reliable system."

Read more: Sean Duffy blames switchover in Arkansas for FAA's ground stop

Equipment 'heart attack'

The new funding request could quickly become another variable in the ongoing negotiations to avoid another shutdown after Dec. 11, when government funding is set to run out. Several Senate Democrats have signaled a willingness in recent weeks to risk a shutdown to pressure President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran.

According to federal officials, the air travel meltdown that disrupted Americans' lives and stranded them at airports was caused by a breakdown in the FAA's communications network. It was prompted by the replacement of a router at a facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, as part of an ongoing effort to switch out old copper wires with fiber-optic cable. Trump and those around him have since blamed the problem on outdated technology.

"I have systems that are from the '90s. I have radar that are from the '60s and '70s," Duffy said on CNN before emphasizing a need for more funding.

Trump weighed in on the situation for the first time Nov. 16.

"Essentially, what you saw on Friday was very, very old equipment that had a heart attack," the president told reporters. He said he was "sure" Congress would soon send more dollars to the FAA.

Duffy to meet with Senate GOP

Duffy is expected to sit in on Senate Republicans' weekly lunch on Nov. 17, where he'll continue to make the case for his funding request.

As of Nov. 16, he had not released comprehensive details on how the $50 billion request would be spent. Before upping his ask, however, Duffy spent the last few months pitching an initial $30 billion.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-Louisiana, who told USA TODAY he'd be supportive of appropriating more money, said he wasn't sure why the request increased "overnight."

"I understand we have inflation, but it's not that dramatic," he said half-jokingly. "They just need to do a better job of explaining it to us."

Retiring Sen. Thom Tillis, R-North Carolina, expressed the same sentiments, saying "people have got to explain to me really even the basis for the $30 billion, let alone the additional $20 billion."

Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he, too, wanted clarification.

"There's some explanations that have to be given as to why that number is where it is," he told reporters. Senate Republicans more broadly have already "attempted to do what we can to ensure that the concerns they have about modernization are being addressed."

Democrats skeptical of unspent funds

Democrats are signaling an early frustration with Duffy's request.

They've spent the last few days pointing to a $12.5 billion allocation in Trump's so-called "One Big, Beautiful Bill" meant specifically for air traffic control system upgrades. According to Washington Rep. Eric Larsen, the top Democrat on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, $11 billion of that remains unspent.

Rep. Rosa DeLauro, the top Democrat on the powerful House Appropriations Committee, called Duffy's funding ask a "$50 billion ransom without a real plan to deliver."

"Congress has shown its willingness to modernize the FAA’s systems and support its workforce as part of annual bipartisan legislation, but we need a competent partner at the Department of Transportation to carry this out in a sustainable, transparent manner," she said in a statement. "Right now, it is clear that we lack such a partner."

Some Republicans have similar questions.

"They have funds available, near as I can tell, that have not been contracted," said Sen. Mike Rounds, R-South Dakota, adding he has questions for Duffy about "why they haven't spent the money they've got."

Duffy has defended the Transportation Department, saying all of that tranche of money will be spent and deployed by the end of 2028. None of the money Congress included in that batch of funding, he argued, could go toward fully replacing new telecommunications architecture.

"They were very specific on how we spend the 12.5, and none of the money goes to this telecom that I have to build," Duffy said on ABC News. "They need to give me additional money to finish that project."

Transportation Department and FAA staff will brief congressional staffers about the latest funding request this week.

Zachary Schermele is the congressional correspondent for USA TODAY. Reach him by email at zschermele@usatoday.com and on Signal @zachschermele.02. Follow him on X at @ZachSchermele.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Ground stop chaos spurs fight in Congress over air traffic control funding

item.title: Nvidia board not considering Huang's return despite mounting pressure, source says
item.description:
By Jaspreet Singh and Ross Kerber

Nov 16 (Reuters) - Four days after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, felled by revelations of affairs including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, an extraordinary campaign is underway to restore him to the helm of the company he built.

More than 180,200 people have signed a petition demanding Huang’s return, Elon ‌Musk has thrown his support behind the effort, and U.S. President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang reinstated as CEO. Thousands of people identifying themselves as Nvidia employees ‌have joined the call, even as governance experts and some investors warn that bringing him back before investigations are complete could expose the company to fresh risks.

The groundswell of support for Huang has turned a corporate succession story into a test of whether ​Nvidia can separate itself from a founder whose influence stretches across its employees — some fiercely loyal to the former CEO — and shareholders, Silicon Valley, the Taiwan supply chain and Washington.

Taiwan's tallest skyscraper, Taipei 101, was illuminated on Monday with messages including "Taiwan Loves Jensen." Some prominent shareholders such as Atreides Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital Management CEO Brad Gerstner have urged Nvidia not to rush to replace him before all the facts were known.

The support for the former CEO comes as U.S. intelligence agencies are still trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's relationship with China’s Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two ‌sources familiar with the matter. Evidence gathered so far indicates she was ⁠likely an intelligence asset, someone who shared information, rather than a fully trained spy, the sources said.

But Nvidia's board was not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The uncertainty has divided investors over Huang's future and complicated the board’s search for a successor. Nvidia shares fell 3.7% ⁠on Monday, a day before the chipmaker is due third-quarter earnings.

WALL STREET STANDS DIVIDED

The "Stand With Jensen" campaign listed SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney among its signatories.

The campaign website showed more than 8,800 signatories identified themselves as current Nvidia employees and more than 94,000 as shareholders, though it cautioned that professional affiliations were self-reported and had not been independently verified.

"We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and ​supporters. ​We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an ​independent investigation establishes the facts," an open letter on the website said.

Huang stepped ‌down on Thursday after reports of alleged affairs with employees, including one who reported directly to him, plunging the AI chip heavyweight into crisis and sending shockwaves through an industry he helped bankroll.

“I think he learned a big lesson,” Trump said on Monday. Trump's reported trades this year suggest he held between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August, the Washington Post reported on Monday, citing a review of his financial disclosures.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, though, has called for Nvidia to appoint an outsider as its next CEO, saying the company needs a "dramatic shake-up" following Huang's departure.

Institutional investors too may prove harder to persuade. Richard Windsor, an independent technology researcher, said he expected large institutional Nvidia investors to oppose Huang’s return while investigations remained unresolved because of the legal exposure and uncertainty it could create.

“They’re very risk-averse,” Windsor ‌said, but said his own view was that Nvidia shareholders would ultimately be better served by Huang’s return because ​of the relationships he has built with the company’s customers and suppliers, particularly TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia’s most advanced chips.

HUANG'S EXIT ​ROCKS TAIWAN

Nowhere is Huang’s unusual reach more visible than in Taiwan, where he was born and ​where Nvidia relies on TSMC and a sprawling network of suppliers to manufacture the chips and systems underpinning the AI boom.

Born in the historic capital of Tainan before ‌moving to the United States as a child, Huang gradually gained celebrity-like status on ​the island, where the wave of adulation surrounding him ​has been dubbed “Jensanity.”

For many Taiwanese, Huang's exit marks the loss of a charismatic champion who helped put the island at the heart of the global artificial intelligence boom, with his influence extending well beyond the technology industry.

Jimmy Yang, 42, who works in marketing, said Huang's departure was a loss for Taiwan, where his influence had extended to local businesses and tourism, and expressed hope ​that Huang could eventually return to Nvidia, drawing a parallel with Apple co-founder ‌Steve Jobs, who returned to the company after being forced out.

"His private life is his own choice," Yang said. "But whether it's the night market economy he's driven or his help ​for the tech industry, it has been massive."

(Reporting by Jaspreet Singh in Bengaluru and Ross Kerber; and additional reporting by Karen Freifeld in New York, Wen-Yee Lee in Taipei ​and Erin Banco in Washington; Writing by Sayantani Ghosh; Editing by Christian Plumb, Anil D'Silva, and Nick Zieminski)

This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/silicon-valley-leaders-back-call-145909540.html

item.title: Chase says transactions are back to normal after outage online and at some branches
item.description:
Chase Bank said transactions were posting normally Monday evening after a nationwide outage that had some customers reporting trouble accessing their accounts and withdrawing funds.

“Transactions are now posting normally,” a Chase spokesperson said around 6:30 p.m.

The outage began Monday morning, according to a source familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak publicly.

Reports began to surface online Monday afternoon from customers across a range of banks saying they were receiving error messages when attempting to perform bank transactions.

Chase said at around 4 p.m. on X that “JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware system” and that it was working to resolve it.

The issues had been affecting both online and in-person branch transactions.

The issue was not “cyber-related,” the bank said, and did not impact the entire banking system. “Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us.”

The bank said that customers still had access to their accounts and funds, but some transactions were taking longer than normal.

Regulators were in touch with the big banks affected “immediately,” a person familiar with the situation said earlier Monday. They “quickly determined this was contained and service was already in process of restoration,” the person said then.

The issues at Chase were the latest in a series of nationwide tech glitches over the past week that have shaken public confidence in systems that tens of millions of Americans use every day. However, there is no evidence that these incidents are connected to one another.

Microsoft Outlook went offline for approximately 48 hours last week due to what it called a capacity upgrade.

On Friday, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for several hours over what U.S. officials said was a botched facilities upgrade.

It was not immediately clear how many Chase accounts were affected by the glitch. The bank counts approximately 94 million customer relationships in the United States, with 5,000 physical branches and 15,000 ATMs.

By late afternoon Monday, several Chase bank branches in Manhattan appeared to be operating normally. Customers leaving a branch at 6th Avenue and W. 51st Street told NBC News they didn’t know there had been a problem until they arrived at the branch, where they were told by employees that they’d gotten there at just the right time.

“This is really retail banking,” and not tied to the rest of JPMorgan Chase, said a source familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak publicly.

The issues with Chase accounts also appeared to be preventing customers from transferring money via Zelle. A representative for the company said that the technical issues on its platform originated with Chase.

“Zelle is not down. Zelle is operating as it should,” the company told NBC News. “An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers. Please contact them directly.”

A representative for U.S. Bank confirmed that Zelle customers were experiencing issues.

“U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted,” the spokesman said. “However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”

A spokesperson for PNC Bank said it was “not experiencing any direct impact. We are aware of reports of transaction delays outside of the bank, but those appear to be resolving.”

Truist bank said its services “are operating normally,We continue to closely monitor our systems and are not aware of any broad service disruptions at this time.”

Customers at Wells Fargo also experienced delays, but the company did not provide a statement.

Citibank likewise declined to comment.

A spokesperson for Capital One said the bank “has not been impacted and continues to operate normally at this time.”

— WMAQ’s Lauren Stauffer and Leigh Lesniak contributed reporting from Chicago.

This article was originally published on NBCNews.com

This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/business/consumer/outages-chase-banking-online-branches-rcna609673

item.title: 'Everybody's shell-shocked': GOP insiders face 2028 prospects after midterm defeats
item.description:
On Election Day, many Republicans were bracing for a tough outcome, but not what has been described as a blue tsunami.

"I thought that we were going to keep the Senate," former Republican National Committee Chair Ronna McDaniel told ABC News. "I didn't think that Democrats could make inroads in states like South Carolina and Kansas and even Texas."

Democrats did more than make inroads. They flipped eight GOP-held Senate seats and as of Monday, Democrats hold 256 House seats to the GOP's 170. There are still some outstanding races as of Monday: nine House races and one Senate race.

Over a dozen Republican donors and operatives told ABC News that the Republican Party is still in shock after the sweeping midterm losses. They pointed to a message that focused on culture wars and failed to reach voters squeezed by costs tied to the war in Iran and a Latino coalition that slipped away. Some argued Vice President JD Vance may no longer be the presumptive 2028 nominee. Vance, who has not formally announced he is launching a presidential bid for 2028, has acknowledged "there's a chance" he won't run in 2028.

'The South is in play': Longtime red states emerge as potential battleground for Democrats

The president’s record-low approval ratings were also difficult to ignore, some said.

"The losses are all about Trump," said one Republican consultant who worked on races out West and spoke to ABC News on the condition of anonymity. "This was a total rebuke of Donald Trump, both him personally and his politics."

RNC National Press Secretary Natalie Baldassarre said in a statement that Republicans will "continue to put America first,” highlighting that the RNC raised $130 million, sending more than $60 million directly to Republican campaigns.

When reached for comment, the White House emphasized Trump’s signature tax legislation and said that Trump will continue to work for the American people.

"Under President Trump’s leadership, this administration has signed the largest working-class tax cuts in history, secured the border, cut the cost of prescription drugs, added more than one million private-sector jobs, and locked in nearly 20 trade deals. President Trump will never stop delivering results for the American people and he will undoubtedly go down as the most successful and consequential president in American history," White House spokesman Davis Ingle told ABC News in a statement.

Vance's office, when asked for comment, deferred to the White House.

A messaging problem

The donors and operatives who spoke to ABC News agreed Republicans lacked a clear message on affordability -- a key issue for voters.

"We need to talk about pocketbook issues. We didn’t do that,” said Sarah Chamberlain, president and CEO of the Republican Main Street Partnership, a group that fundraises for moderate Republicans.

T.W. Arrighi, a Republican strategist who worked on Republican Darline Graham’s Senate race, said Democrats were talking about affordability "in a more tangible way than we were … We have conservative solutions to these issues, we just didn’t deliver."

A GOP strategist involved in many 2026 races said the party's turnout operation will likely take much of the blame. ABC News' analysis of early voting in Texas and Georgia a week before Election Day showed greater Democratic enthusiasm.

"We just weren't hitting the numbers we needed to hit of just sheer Republicans voting. A lot of them stayed home, and we knew that was happening," the strategist said.

The Republican consultant who worked on races out West added that Republicans had "no choice" but to run on culture war issues because of the high costs brought on by the Iran war.

"You can't tell people to ignore your lying eyes,” the source said. "[Republicans] had no choice but to go down the culture-war road because we couldn't talk about the economy."

Trump said in a phone interview with Fox News on election night that he was "a little bit surprised" by the midterm results and added that part of the reason was the Iran war, directly linking it to gas prices.

In a social media post after the election, Trump wrote that Republicans would have been more successful had he been on the ballot.

Reversal among Latino voters

According to the ABC News Voter Poll, in 2026, Latino voters nationally supported Democratic House candidates by a 30-point margin. In 2024, it was a 13-point margin.

Trump acknowledged his mass-deportation policies may have been "too tough" in an interview with CBS News' "60 Minutes" after the midterms.

Mike Madrid, a GOP consultant who studies Latino voting behavior, said "there is no question that the ICE stuff and deportations played a role."

"There’s also no question that the economy was the No. 1 factor. But in some districts, like south Texas, they're one and the same. Immigration is the economy there," Madrid said.

Latino vote helped thwart Texas Republicans' redistricting effort

Democrats swept every congressional district along the southern border, flipping several Republican-held seats in Texas.

Billionaire donor John Catsimatidis told ABC News that the losses came down to the war in Iran and "ICE being too tough on waiters and busboys."

Immigration enforcement under the Trump administration has reached local businesses and restaurants. ABC News reported last May that in D.C., federal law enforcement officials visited dozens of restaurants, carry-out spots and bars across several neighborhoods.

A fight over who leads the RNC

RNC Co-Chair KC Crosbie announced on Nov. 5 that she's challenging RNC Chair Joe Gruters, saying the party should "be willing to confront where we fell short."

A source close to Gruters confirmed to ABC News that he is running for reelection. 

While Trump has since reaffirmed his support for Gruters, some Republicans questioned Gruters' competence.

“Joe Gruters failed the Republican Party, and I find it puzzling that he believes he deserves to be reelected,” said an RNC member.

Florida GOP Chairman Evan Power said in a statement, however, that "Gruters was a key partner in our fight to keep the Free State of Florida red, and he’s the leader I trust to keep our party on offense and ready to win in 2028."

McDaniel said "the committee should support whoever the president wants to be the RNC chair."

She added that donors who may be discouraged from giving in the future need an autopsy from the party over what went wrong.

"People are still wondering what happened, and the sooner that a plan is put forward, and they get in the field and they get data … That's going to be what’s going to bring donors back. But right now, I think everybody's shell-shocked."

The road to 2028

While Vance hasn't ruled out a run in 2028, some donors told ABC News that his proximity to Trump may be a liability.

But a Vance ally who spoke to ABC News cautioned against writing off Vance, comparing it to the 2016 and 2024 election cycles, when different parts of the Republican Party wrote Trump off.

And although Vance is still undecided about a 2028 presidential run, many of Vance's allies expect that he will run for president in 2028, sources confirmed to ABC News Chief Washington Correspondent Jonathan Karl.

Vance's allies say he will decide whether to pursue a White House bid on his own timeline. 

But some Republicans see an opening for Secretary of State Marco Rubio to run for president in 2028 following the midterm elections.

Rubio has said he has no plans to run for president in 2028, adding that he would support Vance if he mounted a presidential run.

Catsimatidis said his family has been supporters of Vance, but he has known Rubio for 15 years and considers the nomination "still open."

A Texas-based GOP donor said the next nominee must appeal to "most all Republicans, a majority of independents and a reasonable group of conservative Democrats."

"We're in like stage two with a five-stage model of grief or something. We're not at the writing-checks-for-new-people yet stage," said one donor. "America doesn't want more MAGA."

This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/Politics/everybodys-shell-shocked-republican-operatives-face-2028-prospects/story?id=138117916

item.title: 美国玩具业等待中美落实关税减免，特朗普与习近平会晤受关注
item.description:
于规模较小的进口商而言，关税政策的不确定性进一步加重了过去两年积累的财务压力。 玩具企业The Queen's Treasures创始人乔安·卡蒂利亚过去两年一直在努力维持公司经营。关税上涨和融资困难使她无力承担原定的生产计划。 为了增加收入，她将位于纽约州北部提康德罗加镇的公司库存仓库改造成零售商店，还推出了精品食品系列，希望在筹集资金的同时，逐步恢复在中国生产的玩具业务。 去年美国对中国商品的关税反复调整，挤压了卡蒂利亚的销售收入。仓库改造成本又给她带来额外负担。 美国与伊朗战争期间，霍尔木兹海峡事实上关闭，造成的航运中断至今仍在影响公司经营。 谈到特朗普的政策，卡蒂利亚说：“这与美国和美国梦完全背道而驰。对我们来说，这简直就是美国噩梦。” 这段经历让她感到愤怒，认为自己的处境根本没有得到政府重视。她希望玩具最终能够根据9月达成的贸易协议获得关税豁免。

item.title: 分析：全球富裕国家移民潮逆转，经济增长与人口老龄化面临新挑战
item.description:
OECD数据显示，2025年37个有统计数据的成员国中有25个永久移民人数下降，流入OECD国家的永久移民总量下降1.6%；若排除西班牙、葡萄牙和意大利，降幅达到8%。国际学生人数也从2023年高峰的210万人降至160万人。 美国、英国、加拿大和澳大利亚等传统目的地收紧工作、留学及人道主义签证，政治上也更难重新放宽移民政策。英国延长获得永久居留的等待时间，加拿大和澳大利亚重点限制国际学生及其他临时居民。 研究模拟显示，若没有移民，到2060年法国、西班牙和德国的劳动年龄人口将比基准预测少逾10%，美国和英国约少20%，加拿大降幅超过30%。经济学家认为，移民可扩大税基、缓解老龄化压力，但快速增长也可能加剧住房和公共服务紧张。 随着英语国家提高门槛，德国、意大利和爱尔兰的大学开始吸引更多国际学生；部分前往美国受阻的拉美移民则转而在墨西哥定居，可能为当地劳动力市场带来新的增长机会。

item.title: FEMA will test a nationwide emergency alert on Tuesday. Your phone won't get it.
item.description:
Be forewarned: On Tuesday afternoon, TVs and radios — not wireless phones — nationwide will blare a jolting emergency alert. But don’t be alarmed; it’s only a test. We repeat: It’s only a test.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), along with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), is running the test to ensure the Emergency Alert System (EAS) for radio and television works during an actual emergency, such as a natural disaster, terrorist attack or other threat to public safety.

Wireless phones will not receive the test alert.

“Wireless Emergency Alerts were tested in 2023, but they will not be part of this year’s test,” according to FEMA. 

It comes amid online conspiracy theories that there will be a 90-day power outage on Tuesday, Nov. 17, particularly following last week’s Microsoft global Outlook outage and the Federal Aviation Administration’s rare ground stop. The federal government has not announced a nationwide 90-day blackout or plans to shut down the U.S. power grid. The rumors are centered around a Pentagon plan to ensure the military has access to critical energy, infrastructure and other resources in case of future disruptions.

Here’s what you can expect and what to know about the FEMA test on Tuesday.

When will the alert test happen?

The nationwide test is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 17, at approximately 2:20 p.m. ET. Here’s when you can expect to be alerted depending on your time zone:

  • 2:20 p.m. ET

  • 1:20 p.m. CT

  • 12:20 p.m. MT

  • 11:20 a.m. PT

  • 10:20 a.m. AT

  • 9:20 a.m. HT

What will the test look and sound like?

Radio and television broadcasters nationwide will interrupt their programming with a message that generally says: “This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. This is only a test. No action is required by the public.”

According to FEMA, the Emergency Alert System involves thousands of independently operated radio, television, cable, satellite and wireline broadband providers. Since they use different equipment, the visual or audio formats may differ by station.

“The test will include alert tones to support accessibility for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing,” according to FEMA. And depending on the broadcaster and their capabilities, the message will be delivered in English, Spanish or both.

How long will the test last?

If your TV or radio is on and tuned to a broadcast station, cable system, satellite radio or television provider, or wireline video service, you should receive the test from the EAS, which is expected to take about one minute.

Why is the national emergency test happening?

Federal law requires FEMA to test the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System (IPAWS) at least once every three years. The last national test was conducted on Oct. 4, 2023.

“If an actual emergency or significant weather event occurs on test day, FEMA and the FCC may postpone the test,” according to FEMA. “The backup date for the nationwide test is December 3, 2026.”

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/fema-will-test-its-emergency-alert-system-tomorrow-heres-what-to-expect-210358652.html

item.title: 金融时报：西方对中国人工智能安全的误解
item.description:
文章认为，西方将中国人工智能安全政策概括为保护中国共产党，忽略了中国监管体系中并存的多种政策取向。中国确实把政治安全、制度安全和意识形态安全置于核心位置，要求面向公众的生成式人工智能符合社会主义核心价值观，并接受算法备案和审查。 但在关键基础设施遭攻击、人工智能失控等领域，中国近期发布的风险报告和安全框架，与西方政策讨论存在相近之处，均强调部署前评估、持续监测和验证。 中国还通过社会事件和司法实践回应人工智能带来的就业、自残风险及人身和财产损害。最高人民法院一项裁定称，自动驾驶、价格歧视等应用造成损害时，生产商和销售商可能承担赔偿责任。作者据此呼吁美国不要以对中国安全关切的简化认识，回避制定国际人工智能标准。

item.title: 美股收盘：纳指暴跌2.5%，英伟达危机引发科技股抛售，黄金白银与比特币同步下跌
item.description:
美股周一大幅下跌，纳斯达克指数跌2.49%，标普500指数跌1.92%，道指跌1.41%。英伟达因黄仁勋离职后的管理层危机，以及美国收紧人工智能芯片出口限制，下跌4.12%。 抛售从半导体和人工智能相关企业蔓延至金融股，美联储进一步加息的预期也加重了市场压力。黄金和白银期货双双创52周新低，比特币徘徊在6.4万美元附近，国际油价同样走低。 华尔街多家机构下调英伟达、戴尔等企业的目标价，但摩根士丹利仍预计标普500指数到2027年底有约15%的上涨空间。瑞银认为人工智能投资周期尚未结束，但提醒投资者关注企业盈利和融资风险。 本周英伟达财报、Anthropic计划进行的IPO以及美联储会议纪要，将成为决定市场短期走势的重要因素。

item.title: 加拿大保守党领袖波利耶夫办公室至少五名核心幕僚将离职
item.description:
加拿大保守党领袖波利耶夫办公室至少五名核心幕僚已告知准备离职，其中包括副幕僚长兼政策主管亚伦·伍德里克，以及两名高级传播负责人米卡·格林和萨姆·利利。格林和利利将转往新当选的卑诗省保守党政府任职，伍德里克则计划进入私营部门。 这轮变动将使官方反对党领袖办公室在政策制定和新闻传播方面出现人事空缺。该办公室今年早些时候也已有前幕僚长和前传播主管离任。 波利耶夫同时面对议员流失和12月联邦补选压力。自2025年大选以来，保守党已有九名议员离开原有职位或发生身份变化；六个补选选区中有两个原由保守党控制，其中安大略省布兰特福德及南布兰特选区因独立候选人参选和自由党支持率上升而竞争趋于激烈。保守党内部人士称，目前没有发动行动罢免波利耶夫的计划。

item.title: Tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz as 3rd U.S. aircraft carrier arrives
item.description:
Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.

Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities.

See the most recent developments below.

Latest Developments


Nov 16, 5:10 PM
Another tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz: UKMTO

A second tanker was reported attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre.

The incident was reported north of Khasab, Oman, according to an UKMTO alert.

"A third-party has reported an attack involving a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz, disabling the vessel and resulting in an engine room fire," the alert stated. "The crew have been reported safe. Damage assessment, and environmental impact are unknown at the time of this report."

Nov 16, 8:46 AM
Saudi Arabia intercepts 2 Houthi drones, spokesperson says

Saudi Arabia intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia on Monday, according to the spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government in that country's civil war.

The drones were intercepted over the Mecca and Riyadh regions, the spokesperson said.

-ABC News' Victoria Beaule

Nov 16, 6:50 AM
Bahrain jails 64 people over alleged IRGC terror plot

A Bahrain court sentenced 64 people to between 15 years and life in prison on Monday, accusing them of establishing a terror group linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Their sentencing comes after Iran resumed drone attacks against Bahrain on Friday and Sunday. Manama said both attacks were defeated by the kingdom's air defenses.

-ABC News' Victoria Beaule

Nov 16, 3:43 AM
Tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre reported an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz early on Monday morning.

"The company security officer of a tanker has reported the vessel being struck by an unknown projectile whilst transiting outbound," the alert said. "This resulted in a fire in the engine room. No casualties have been reported and all crew have been accounted for."

Nov 15, 5:24 PM
3rd US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East

A third aircraft carrier strike group has arrived in the Middle East, a U.S. official told ABC News.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier strike group entered the U.S. Central Command area of operations earlier Sunday, the official said.

The carrier strike group now joins the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington, which have been operating in the Arabian Sea.

They are among the more than 20 U.S. Navy ships enforcing the blockade of Iranian ports.

-ABC News' Luis Martinez

Nov 15, 4:55 PM
Oil tanker struck mine near Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, IRGC claims

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said in a statement Sunday that an oil tanker struck naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, according to the state-run Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA).

The tanker had switched off its navigation systems and was attempting to pass through "a restricted zone," the IRGC navy statement said.

The IRGC statement did not include images of the alleged incident.

-ABC News' Somayeh Malekian

Nov 15, 7:00 AM
Bahrain says Iran 'fully responsible' for latest attacks

Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that it holds Iran "fully responsible" for drone attacks targeting the Gulf kingdom on Friday and Sunday, describing the incidents as constituting "a resumption of Iran's aggression against Bahrain and other countries in the region."

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for both attacks, which Manama said were defeated by the kingdom's air defense systems.

Tehran has warned that any regional nations assisting U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran will be considered legitimate targets. Bahrain and other U.S.-aligned Gulf states have traditionally hosted American military personnel and bases.

Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said it rejects "the use of its territory to settle accounts and holds Iran fully responsible for the attacks and their consequences."

Click here to read the rest of the blog.This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/International/live-updates/iran-live-updates-tanker-attacked-strait-hormuz-ukmto/?id=138171071

item.title: Ex-Commerce Dept. staffers say there was a lack of enforcement under Lutnick
item.description:
Some former Commerce Department officials are describing Howard Lutnick's tenure as secretary as being marked by "chaos," "micromanaging," and what they allege are failures to act on evidence of highly sensitive computer chip smuggling.

A key national security responsibility of the department is investigating and enforcing bans on the export to China and other U.S. adversaries of advanced computer chips used in artificial intelligence and sophisticated weapons. 

"There was an inexplicable refusal to use the tools at their disposal for national security over the last year," one former Commerce official told CBS News.

Scrutiny of Lutnick's tenure has heightened in recent days with Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO after admitting an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believed to be a Chinese spy. China has denied the accusation of spying, calling it "an attempt to smear China."

As the scandal has unfolded, senior officials and members of Congress have questioned how Nvidia was permitted to sell chips to companies with deep ties to China, and whether the Commerce Department policed those exports effectively.

The answer, according to some of Lutnick's former staff, was not at all.

Four ex-Commerce officials spoke with CBS News, asking to remain anonymous, fearing professional reprisals for discussing their recent experience in government.

"We weren't able to add entities to the Entity List. That was just a complete stop," one former Commerce employee said, referring to the federal list of firms that the U.S. government has banned from buying the most advanced chips due to the belief they would route them to China or other adversaries.

Another former Commerce official said a whole year passed with no companies added to the list, noting that this was the first time that had happened in 18 years. The Federal Register shows the last time entities were added was Oct. 9, 2025, and the last yearlong gap in additions was in 2008.

The first former staffer said the agency's own enforcement officers found suspicious activity at Southeast Asian sites where Nvidia chips had been delivered, but that Commerce directors allegedly took no action.

Placement on the list triggers more stringent license requirements and creates a higher threshold to prevent sensitive products from getting where they shouldn't, the ex-official said. 

Instead, "nothing happened," the ex-official said.

The Biden administration issued AI chip export controls in 2022 and 2023, and in January 2025 issued an interim final rule to block China and other adversaries from obtaining the most advanced AI chips, both directly and through third-party countries.

In May 2025, President Trump's Commerce Department rolled back the rule, arguing it "would have stifled American innovation." Instead, the department said it would strengthen export controls for AI chips by issuing guidance to the industry and public.

There are growing signs that bans on exporting advanced U.S. computer chips have been circumvented in large quantities, according to published reports.

An April 2026 study by AI research nonprofit Epoch estimated between 290,000 and 1.6 million cutting-edge AI chips were smuggled into China in 2024 and 2025, comprising "roughly a quarter of the comput[ing power] China acquired through legal channels or domestic production." 

Tech news site The Information reported that at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips allegedly ended up with Chinese companies since 2023 just through companies linked to Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese agent accused of an affair with Nvidia's ousted CEO. The report cited sources close to her for the estimate.

And a former researcher at OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, published a paper last week claiming to have found digital forensic evidence that top Chinese AI models were trained using Nvidia chips banned in China.

One former Commerce staffer described the department under Lutnick as "very chaotic, very frantic," with staff sometimes learning of major policy changes via media reports, including a pivot to allow the sale of Nvidia's H20 and H200 chips to China — the company's second-most advanced tier of GPUs.

"We found out about that in The New York Times," the ex-Commerce official said. "It was pretty clear that the decision was made between Trump and Jensen Huang."

The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.  CBS News has also reached out to the White House for comment.

On Monday the department imposed a new rule requiring licenses for exporting, re-exporting or transferring advanced semiconductors to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore or Thailand, aimed at closing a loophole through which chips were exported to China via an intermediary. But the Commerce Department suggested that its own involvement was limited, describing the rule as "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council—to address remote access to advanced super intelligence (SI) chips and servers."

The department lost two of its most senior and experienced experts shortly after Lutnick took office.

One was Matthew Borman, who served as principal deputy assistant secretary for export administration. Borman had been with the department for over 30 years.

Another veteran official, Eileen Albanese, was let go from her longtime role as director of the Office of National Security Controls. Reuters first reported their departures in February 2025, the same month Lutnick started running the department.

"They kicked off the administration by essentially firing the two most respected people," said one former employee. 

A profile on the website of law firm Akin Gump, where Albanese now works, says she played a "key role in the development of U.S. export control policy and regulations for advanced artificial intelligence chips and semiconductor manufacturing tools."

"Matt and Eileen were treasures of the U.S. government," one former Commerce staffer said.

Albanese did not respond to a request for comment. Borman declined to comment.

Former officials said subsequent changes under Lutnick helped prompt an "exodus" of up to 50 skilled staff members over the past 18 months.

Over time, those who departed were among the most experienced officials who dealt with key areas including chips and export control enforcement, the ex-staffers said.

"It was an exodus of the finest engineers and scientists, the key experts on AI, on Russia, on diversion, our key expert on chips. Decades of institutional memory and skill went out," an ex-employee said.

Key roles remain vacant in Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, the department in charge of export controls, according to a registry of current senior federal employees. The principal deputy assistant secretary for export administration, the same role for export enforcement and the chief of staff roles are all currently unfilled, the records say.

Some staff described a bottleneck at the Bureau of Industry and Security, accusing its chief — Jeffrey Kessler, a top deputy to Lutnick — of "micromanaging" and blocking enforcement against companies suspected of smuggling chips.

"He made everything go through him. Literally every possible decision, the most minor things. It's impossible for one person to manage that level of things," one former employee under Lutnick told CBS News.

"He didn't want to make any decisions on his own. He would want you to make a memo and he would say, 'Package it up with options for me to bring to a decision maker,' which always cracked me up. Because it's like, who are you? A concerned citizen?"

"The career workforce felt frustrated and stymied," said one former staffer from the previous administration, who is close to many who remained in the department. "They felt like they were unable to do their jobs because [Kessler and Lutnick] were standing in their way."

The former staff members told CBS News that the critical view of Lutnick and his deputy was widely shared in the department. 

Cabinet members have even voiced criticism, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent telling CNBC last week that Lutnick failed to follow through on chip ban enforcement supported by Treasury, the State Department and others in the administration.

"Commerce has the pen. You would have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent told the channel.

"I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above" a certain sophistication, Bessent said.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/howard-lutnick-commerce-department-chips-chaos-former-employees/

item.title: 邓聿文：习近平如何看待政治地位削弱的特朗普
item.description:
按照中国方面的理解，这也释放出一种信号：华盛顿开始接受中国作为平等战略大国的地位，并愿意将双边竞争限制在一定范围内。 北京显然希望，“尊重”和“战略稳定”等原则能够延伸至中国认为涉及核心利益的问题，特别是台湾和技术领域。 但特朗普接受这些外交措辞，并不代表整个美国政治体系都认同这一框架。 特朗普本人甚至可能并不理解中方措辞所包含的深层含义。 对华盛顿而言，战略稳定更多是指管控冲突、保护美国利益，以及维护自身的竞争优势。

item.title: 八十年代川大的研究生宿舍生活
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

1984年秋，我在四川大学本科毕业后继续读研究生。那时的川大还没有与成都科技大学和四川医学院合并，全校博士、硕士研究生加起来只有一百多人，基本都住在五舍。

五舍是一栋老旧的四层筒子楼。研究生住不满，一些年轻教师也住在那里。楼前有洗衣台和球场，离大礼堂、外文楼都不远，旁边就是女生宿舍六舍，地理位置很好。

但住宿条件实在谈不上好。

楼道墙皮斑驳，一楼阴暗潮湿，厕所设在每层楼中间，气味常年飘在走廊里。水房也和厕所挨在一起，只隔一道矮墙。夏天最难受，开窗有臭味，关窗又闷热，只能轮流忍受。

楼里的老鼠也很多。

有一次，无线电系的金羽正在宿舍吃饭，一只老鼠从天花板上掉到桌上，把饭碗撞翻。他一怒之下买来鼠药，第二天果然毒死了一只大老鼠。为了抗议宿舍卫生状况，他把死老鼠钉在一楼广告栏上，旁边写了一张纸条：“世界卫生组织收。”

结果早晨下楼吃饭的同学看到以后，有人当场吐了出来。后来清洁工把死老鼠和污物收拾掉，这场“行为艺术”才结束。

五舍虽然破旧，却也有自己的生活气息。

楼前洗衣台经常聚着研究生和年轻教师。大家洗衣服、聊天，年轻男女也会在那里认识。有些后来成为情侣的人，最初就是从洗衣台旁边几句闲聊开始的。

1985年秋，新建成的新一舍投入使用，我们84级研究生也搬了过去。

相比五舍，新一舍几乎称得上是改善住房。

新楼有七层，房间宽敞，厕所、水源和卫生条件都比过去好得多。研究生宿舍通常两三个人一间。我更幸运，两个室友都是成都人，平时住在家里，寝室大部分时间只有我一个人。

本科时，宿舍主要用来睡觉，每天从教室到食堂、图书馆来回奔忙。读研究生以后，生活节奏完全不同。寝室既是住处，也是读书、聊天、下棋和接待朋友的地方。

新一舍前面有一大片水泥空地。每天吃饭前后，总有许多学生站在那里聊天。春秋天气好的时候，更是三五成群。研究生人数少，彼此很快就熟悉了。

那时候，研究生每个月有五十多元生活补贴，有的人还在外面代课挣一点钱。三四个人偶尔去校外小饭馆吃顿饭，点几样川菜，再喝点生啤，十来块钱就可以吃得很好。

校园舞会也是那个年代研究生生活的重要部分。

经济系一位同学会拉手风琴，又组织了几个会乐器的研究生，成立了一个小乐队。最初说是参加文艺演出，后来最大的用途却是给舞会伴奏。

那时候成都高校里的舞会刚刚流行起来，多数是在食堂或露天场地举行。我们却借附近中学的场地，用乐队现场伴奏，参加者也基本是熟人邀请来的。

一段时间里，几乎每周都有舞会。

后来乐队的主要组织者因为工作单位评职称回了家乡，正式舞会慢慢停了，我们又把舞会搬到寝室里。把桌椅挪开，中间腾出一点地方，几个男生邀请几个女生，在录音机的音乐里跳舞、聊天。

地方很小，反而更容易交谈。

大家聊文学、哲学、历史，有时把弗洛伊德、萨特、李白、杜甫挂在嘴边。现在想起来多少有点年轻人的卖弄，但那确实是当时研究生生活的一部分。

也有人就是在这样的舞会上认识了后来陪伴一生的人。

我的朋友H学先秦文学，一次舞会上认识了学考古的L。两个人边跳舞边谈专业，很快熟悉起来，后来谈恋爱、结婚，一直生活在一起。

那时候研究生大多有自行车，因为要出去代课、参加活动，也方便约会。H有一辆不知道转过几手的旧自行车，刹车已经不太灵，却经常骑着它带L在成都街头到处跑。

有一次两人看电影回来，在九眼桥附近看到一家新开的冰激凌店。H以为两块钱足够，进去以后才知道两个冰激凌要五块钱。身上钱不够，只好向老板解释自己是川大学生。老板最后摆摆手：“算球啦，你们走吧。”

几十年以后说起这件事，大家仍然会笑。

新一舍也并非没有麻烦。

后来成都供电紧张，学校规定研究生宿舍晚上十二点统一熄灯。本科生十一点断电，研究生已经算受到优待，但大家仍然不满。

到了十二点，整栋楼突然黑下来，过不了多久，一扇扇窗户里又亮起蜡烛。

有人继续看书，有人下棋，有人聊天。研究生不像本科生那样完全按照学校规定的时间生活，十二点以后往往才是一天真正安静下来的时候。

新一舍还有一个有趣的问题：几个单元之间不能直接相通。住在高层的人如果想到旁边单元找朋友，必须下到一楼，再从另一个楼梯重新爬上去。

有人嫌麻烦，干脆把两个单元之间的隔墙凿了一个洞，形成一条“秘密通道”。后来女生觉得来往的人太多，影响安全和清静，向学校反映，洞很快又被堵上了。

现在回头看，八十年代的研究生生活当然远没有今天方便。

没有电脑，没有网络，宿舍破旧，新楼也会停电，出门靠自行车，跳舞还要自己找场地、组织乐队。

但那个时期也有一种很特别的气氛。

研究生人数很少，大家来自不同专业，却很容易认识。学习、恋爱、舞会、下棋、骑自行车逛成都，全混在一起。

后来，五舍拆掉了，新一舍也一批又一批换了主人。当年住在那里的人，有的去了国外，有的回到家乡，有的人已经去世。

留下来的，是那些看起来很普通的生活片段。

一栋旧宿舍，一场小舞会，一辆破自行车，一次几块钱都付不起的冰激凌，以及一群刚刚告别大学本科、以为人生才刚刚开始的年轻人。

资料来源：黄文泉《当年川大研究生，风花雪月新一舍》；本文据作者回忆整理改写。

研究生

寸铭河

item.title: 胡塞武装逼近亚丁 沙特更换也门联军指挥官
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

沙特阿拉伯11月16日更换了领导也门军事联军的指挥官。此前，伊朗支持的胡塞武装在战略要地曼德海峡附近取得新的领土进展，迫使沙特支持的也门政府军撤退。

沙特王室命令将联军指挥官法赫德·萨勒曼中将调任国防部顾问，并任命总参谋长鲁瓦伊利接任。官方没有说明人事调整是否直接涉及近期战事失利。

也门政府军15日承认，已从杜巴布机场及曼德海峡附近地区撤出。政府军称这是根据战场形势作出的重新部署，胡塞武装则宣布控制相关地区。

曼德海峡连接红海与亚丁湾，是全球重要航运通道。胡塞武装重新控制附近沿岸地区，增加了地区海上交通面临的安全风险。

与此同时，沙特联军表示，近日连续拦截多架胡塞武装向利雅得、麦加及麦地那地区发射的无人机。

胡塞武装还指责联军袭击也门首都萨那，造成一名儿童死亡、七名平民受伤，相关伤亡数字尚未得到独立核实。

沙特支持的也门政府目前以亚丁为主要据点。胡塞武装近期的军事进展，使也门南部战局及红海航运安全再次受到关注。

关键词: 
胡塞武装
沙特
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 特斯拉拟投资30亿欧元扩建德国工厂
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国电动汽车制造商特斯拉11月16日宣布，计划投资30亿欧元扩建位于德国勃兰登堡州格林海德的欧洲超级工厂，目标是将其建设为集团技术最先进的生产基地，并实现每年最多生产100万辆Cybercab无人驾驶出租车。

扩建项目包括新建生产厂房及污水处理等配套设施，预计2027年上半年动工，2029年投产。特斯拉计划新增数百个工作岗位。该工厂目前约有12600名员工，近几个月已增聘2000人，以扩大电池生产能力。

勃兰登堡州州长沃伊德克欢迎投资计划，认为这表明德国仍具备吸引大型工业项目的能力。

特斯拉德国工厂于2022年投产，此前扩建计划曾因森林砍伐、水资源及交通问题遭到当地居民反对，并引发环保人士抗议。

此次投资计划公布之际，德国传统汽车制造业正面临需求疲软及产业转型压力。特斯拉计划扩大德国生产规模，但Cybercab的实际市场需求及未来量产进度仍有待观察。

item.title: 美军第三艘航母抵达中东 加强对伊朗军事压力
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国中央司令部11月16日证实，“西奥多·罗斯福”号核动力航空母舰已于15日进入中央司令部责任区，成为目前部署在中东的第三艘美国航母。

美军表示，罗斯福号正在执行例行部署任务。该舰与“乔治·华盛顿”号及“乔治·H.W.布什”号共同支持美国对伊朗港口和石油码头实施的海上封锁。

与此同时，巴林政府表示，近日连续拦截来自伊朗的无人机袭击。巴林是美国海军第五舰队司令部所在地，也是美军在波斯湾的重要军事基地。

美国近期还宣布扩大对伊朗补给路线的限制，涉及陆路及里海运输，试图进一步切断伊朗军事物资供应。

川普此前表示，美国目前不需要与伊朗达成协议，将继续维持现有军事压力。伊朗则警告美国不要升级冲突，并表示将采取自卫行动。

美国海军专业媒体指出，罗斯福号原计划接替华盛顿号，三艘航母同时部署可能涉及正常轮换。目前尚不清楚这一部署是否会长期维持。

航母
伊朗

item.title: 南京“零元面馆”之争：不应苛刻对待善心
item.description:
2026-11-17 08:00:00


 农健/插画


2026年10月，张先生在南京市江宁区和雨花台区开了两家“零元面馆”，免费提供一碗素面，外加一些素菜，吸引了不少老人、零工、骑手等排队吃面。张先生接受澎湃新闻采访时表示，他的初衷是请大家吃一碗面，没有其他商业企图。

这本是一件善事，却引起了激烈的争议甚至反对。有人认为零元面馆对周边的小饭馆形成了冲击，“扰乱市场秩序”。有人甚至说，免费供应餐食显然低于成本价，是违法的不正当价格行为。好在主管部门明确表示，免费供餐不属于有偿服务，不适用价格法。

据澎湃新闻报道，雨花台区零元面馆周边有火锅店、咖啡店等，他们普遍表示零元面馆对自家生意没有影响。江宁区那家店开在片区知名的零工集散地，周边有一些小餐馆。正是这些餐馆认为自己生意受影响，反应强烈。但记者看到旁边一家牛肉汤店，从10月8日（零元面馆开业日期）到11月8日一个月时间，营业额比此前一个月还高，日均超过1000元。其他店家虽然声称自家生意腰斩，但不肯向记者展示其营业额。

按常理说，零元面馆会分流一部分可能到其他餐馆就餐的人，但影响到底有多大，恐怕很难说。光顾零元面馆的，主要是周边的老人，还有少部分外卖骑手、环卫工人、零工人员等。其中比例很大的老人，即使不吃零元面馆，恐怕也是在家自己做饭。外卖骑手时间紧张，排队吃免费面的也是少数。

即使其他餐馆生意确实变差，也可能与当地产业变迁、外来务工人员减少有关。澎湃新闻就报道，根据江宁区政府官网信息，近年来该零工市场日均流动求职人员规模在200人以上，相比以往日均300人的流动有较大收缩。

退一步说，零元面馆即使对周边餐馆的生意造成了一定影响，也不能因此否定慈善。据澎湃新闻报道，来零元面馆吃面的，有外地到南京打零工的大龄阿姨，如果一时没找到工作，最低10元一顿的餐费对她来说也是不小的负担，零元面馆就解了她的燃眉之急；对一些生活拮据的外卖小哥和工资不高的小区保安，零元面馆也能让他们每月省下三五百块钱餐费。

如果说零元面馆是扰乱市场秩序，让其他从业者少赚了钱，不应该开下去，那所有的慈善都会挤压市场需求，所有的慈善甚至便民服务都不应该存在，连优惠促销也不该有。毕竟地铁口免费借用的雨具，也会影响便利店的雨伞生意。

有人质疑零元面馆开办者的动机，怀疑其可能用慈善做噱头获取关注和流量，从其他方面获益，甚至收集个人信息用于违法活动。现在社交网络上这样的套路层出不穷，部分网民有这样的怀疑也情有可原。但零元面馆开了已经有一个月，开办者并没有被发现在网上主动进行宣传甚或炒作，零元面馆也没有要求用餐者扫码填写个人信息之类。

此事之所以成为网络热点，是先有媒体报道，后有网民跟进质疑，才形成的。批评应该论迹不论心，在没有任何事实依据的情况下猜测开办者有不良居心，这是诛心之论。即便开办者因为零元面馆获得了关注，从其他方面获取了利益，只要不违法，以其他合法收入来支持零元面馆办下去，又有什么不好呢？

还有观点认为零元面馆不加区分地向所有人免费，会让很多并不贫困的人占便宜，是浪费慈善资源，应该更精准识别受助者，让慈善真正帮助更有需要的人。其实很多慈善行为，几乎都会引起类似的争议。对政府财政帮扶或以募捐为主要来源的慈善机构来说，尽可能选择最恰当的受助对象当然有必要。但拿自己的钱做慈善的人，有权决定用什么方式资助什么人。何况如前文所述，零元面馆的就餐者中，有不少打零工的低收入群体，在城市里，他们就是贫困者。

而要筛选出让所有人都满意的贫困受助者，也是需要付出很高成本的。目前零元面馆在压力之下，调整了免费供餐范围，只向60岁以上的老年人、残障人士、环卫工人、快递员、外卖员提供。是否60岁以上，需要看身份证鉴别，环卫工人、快递员、外卖员可以看工装，但是也不能排除有人买身衣服去蹭吃的可能，要真正鉴别真假，不是件容易的事。

零元面馆是一件善事，只要没有以此行不法之事，没有食品安全问题，就应该坚定支持。对民间行善过于苛刻，会寒了行善者的心，让后来者心生畏惧，不敢行善，让慈善事业受阻。希望有关部门不屈服于压力，支持零元面馆，也希望零元面馆能顶住压力开下去，持续给有需要的人带来温暖。

item.title: 金正恩考察朝鲜北部边境旅游区建设工作
item.description: 韩联社首尔11月17日电 据朝中社17日报道，朝鲜国务委员会委员长金正恩15日至16日对北部的三池渊市旅游园区建设项目进行现场指导。

item.title: 快讯：俄高官称日俄首脑或借APEC之机对话
item.description: 【共同社莫斯科11月17日电】俄罗斯总统新闻秘书佩斯科夫16日表示，“不排除”总统普京与日本首相高市早苗借18日在中国开幕的亚太经合组织（APEC）首脑会议之机对话的可能性。塔斯社对此进行了报道。（完）

item.title: 英国向海外派遣网络部队 主动追踪敌对黑客
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

英国军方已向海外派遣专门网络作战人员，与伙伴国家合作追踪和阻止敌对黑客活动，试图在网络攻击发生前识别并消除威胁。

英国国防网络与电磁部队指挥官迈克·费耶斯少将透露，军方正在海外部署“网络猎敌部队”，加强主动网络防御能力。英国国防部确认有关部署，但拒绝透露具体行动地点、合作国家及目标。

英国近年来多次发生重大网络安全事件。2024年，英国政府指责与中国有关联的黑客组织入侵选举机构，并针对国会议员展开网络侦察。中国否认有关指控。

英国国家网络安全中心2026年度报告显示，报告期内共收到1831起网络安全事件，其中337起需要该中心介入处理，但这些事件并非全部与中国有关。

英国国防部没有确认此次海外行动专门针对中国。网络安全专家认为，相关行动可能包括协助盟国发现并清除隐藏在当地网络中的敌对活动，但应取得东道国同意。

英国政府希望通过提前发现和干扰网络攻击，降低军事系统及关键基础设施面临的风险。

关键词: 
英国
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 快讯：2架疑似俄罗斯军机进入福冈近海日本领空
item.description: 【共同社11月17日电】日本防卫省17日发布消息称，可能是俄罗斯军机的2架飞机当天接连进入福冈县附近海域领空。航空自卫队战机紧急升空并发出警告。（完）

item.title: 美国众议院两党呼吁重建关键制造业
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国众议院美中战略竞争特设委员会11月13日发布两党联合报告，指中国通过政府补贴、国有企业、产业基金及监管政策扩大制造业优势，削弱美国工业基础，并使全球供应链更加依赖中国。报告呼吁美国持续投资，重建关键产业生产能力。

报告由委员会共和党主席穆勒纳尔和民主党首席成员康纳共同发布，重点研究半导体、生物制造、航空航天和机床四大行业。

报告援引集邦咨询数据称，中国占全球成熟制程晶圆代工产能的比例，预计将从2024年的34%上升至2027年的约47%。不过，中国商用飞机仍依赖西方发动机及航空电子设备，高端机床也存在进口依赖。

报告强调，制造业实力直接关系到军事装备补充及长期作战能力，建议美国联合盟友发展供应链、技术和产业人才，并跨越多个政府任期持续推进再工业化战略。

关键词: 
制造业
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 黄仁勋骤然离场，亚洲失去驻美“AI大使”
item.description:
黄瑞黎, ADAM SATARIANO, XINYUN WU, RIVER AKIRA DAVIS
2026年11月17日

In Indonesia, Jensen Huang was called the leader of the artificial intelligence revolution. In Japan, he was “the next Steve Jobs,” according to the technology investor Masayoshi Son. In Taiwan, where he was born, he is just called Dad.

在印度尼西亚，黄仁勋被誉为人工智能革命的领军人物。在日本，科技投资人孙正义称他为“下一个史蒂夫·乔布斯”。在他出生的台湾，人们直接叫他“爸爸”。

Mr. Huang, who resigned this week from the powerhouse Silicon Valley chip company Nvidia, was celebrated across Asia — from South Korea to Japan, Indonesia to Kazakhstan. He traveled frequently to the region, cultivating close ties with business leaders and wooing government officials.

从韩国到日本，从印度尼西亚到哈萨克斯坦，上周从硅谷芯片巨头英伟达辞职的黄仁勋曾在亚洲各地广受赞誉。他频繁前往该地区，与商界领袖建立密切联系，并争取政府官员的支持。

Outside of China, he pitched Nvidia chips as a path to “sovereign A.I.,” the idea that countries had to build their own A.I. supercomputers and data centers, a vision that many government leaders bought into.

在中国以外，他将英伟达芯片推销为通往“主权人工智能”的路径，即各国必须建设自己的人工智能超级计算机和数据中心。许多政府领导人接受了这一愿景。

Even in China, where the business relationships he forged for Nvidia were made more complicated by the rivalry between Beijing and Washington, Mr. Huang was often seen as a bridge. That role was cast in a new light by the explosive revelations about his relationship with a woman the U.S. government believes was spying for China.

在中国，他为英伟达建立的商业关系因中美竞争而变得更加复杂，即便如此，黄仁勋在那里也常被视为一座桥梁。然而，有关他与一名被美国政府认定为中国从事间谍活动的女性之间关系的爆炸性披露，使他的这一角色呈现出新的面貌。

Nvidia is valued at about $4 trillion, one of the largest corporate valuations in the world. Now Mr. Huang’s sudden departure from the company hangs over the region’s technology industry, raising questions about what it portends for the region’s A.I. boom, U.S. policy on China and the continued expansion of data centers in Southeast Asia, where Nvidia chips power A.I. development throughout the region.

英伟达估值约4万亿美元，是全球市值最高的公司之一。如今，黄仁勋突然离开公司，给该地区科技行业蒙上阴影，人们不禁质疑，这对该地区的人工智能热潮、美国对华政策，以及东南亚数据中心的持续扩张意味着什么——在东南亚，英伟达的芯片正推动着整个地区的人工智能发展。

For China, Mr. Huang’s exit could accelerate a drive toward self-sufficiency as Beijing and Chinese companies fear Washington will tighten export controls on American-designed chips.

对中国而言，黄仁勋的离职可能加速中国迈向自给自足的步伐，因为北京和中国企业担心华盛顿将收紧对美国设计芯片的出口管制。

Many Chinese companies use data centers in Malaysia and other countries to access chips they would not otherwise be able to bring into China. In recent days, Chinese companies in Malaysia have begun racing to lease space inside data centers with advanced American-designed A.I. chips before any new restrictions can be put in place, said a data center executive in Malaysia, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss the ongoing efforts.

许多中国公司利用马来西亚和其他国家的数据中心获取原本无法运入中国的芯片。马来西亚一名数据中心高管说，近日，在马来西亚的中国公司已开始争相在装有美国设计先进人工智能芯片的数据中心内租赁空间，以防新限制出台。这名高管要求匿名讨论正在进行的工作。

China had already been positioning itself to be self-sufficient in chips, but many of its companies doing frontier A.I. development relied on Nvidia chips. Mr. Huang’s resignation has pushed up the timeline, according to analysts.

中国此前已在推动芯片自给自足，但许多从事前沿人工智能开发的中国公司依赖英伟达芯片。分析人士称，黄仁勋辞职加快了这一进程。

“The Chinese A.I. industry must prepare for the worst-case scenario: pairing domestic chips with domestic models and building a complete, self-contained ecosystem,” said Zhong Yang, an investor focused on A.I. who is based in Guangdong Province, in an email.

“中国人工智能产业必须为最坏情况做准备：将国产芯片与国产模型配对，构建完整、自足的生态系统，”位于广东省、专注于人工智能的投资者钟阳（音）在电子邮件中表示。

Companies could soon face an “existential necessity” to replace foreign chips with ones made in China, he said.

他说，企业可能很快面临一种“生存必需”，要用中国制造的芯片取代外国芯片。

In China, Mr. Huang was seen as a moderating force on contentious questions about access to advanced technology. He has long argued that strict U.S. export controls would open the doors for more Chinese competition. He has said exporting the “American tech stack” is vital to winning the A.I. race and that the blocking of chip exports forces China away from American technology.

在中国，黄仁勋被视为在获取先进技术这一争议问题上的温和力量。他长期主张，美国严格的出口管制将为更多中国竞争对手打开大门。他说，出口“美国技术栈”对赢得人工智能竞赛至关重要，而阻止芯片出口将迫使中国远离美国技术。

“His departure means that China has lost an influential advocate within the U.S. tech sector for business cooperation,” said Poe Zhao, an independent China technology analyst.

“他的离职意味着中国在美国科技界失去了一位主张商业合作的有影响力的倡导者，”独立中国科技分析师坡·赵（音）说。

Mr. Zhao said he believes that Mr. Huang’s resignation could hurt China’s A.I. industry in the short term, but may benefit domestic chip manufacturers such as Huawei. But he pointed out that Chinese-made chips still lag in performance.

坡·赵说，他认为黄仁勋的辞职短期内可能伤害中国人工智能产业，但可能有利于华为等国内芯片制造商。但他指出，中国制造芯片在性能上仍然落后。

“In the long run, whether China can benefit depends on whether domestically produced chips can truly narrow the technological gap,” he added.

“从长远看，中国能否受益取决于国产芯片能否真正缩小技术差距，”他还说。

Joe Mazur, a senior analyst at Trivium China, a consultancy, said Mr. Huang’s departure could “embolden the voices in Washington that are less in favor of cooperation, more in favor of a hard-line approach.”

咨询公司Trivium China高级分析师乔·马祖尔说，黄仁勋离职可能“助长华盛顿那些不那么支持合作、更倾向于强硬立场的声音”。

Over time, Mr. Huang’s departure is a “dream scenario for China,” said Dan Ives, a prominent technology analyst on Wall Street.

华尔街知名科技分析师丹·艾夫斯说，从长远来看，黄仁勋离职是“中国梦想中的场景”。

“The biggest gating factor between the U.S. and China was Jensen and Nvidia,” Mr. Ives said.

“美中之间最大的关键制约因素就是黄仁勋和英伟达，”艾夫斯说。

One of the distinguishing features of Mr. Huang’s role in the Asia tech world was his ability to cultivate personal relationships with Nvidia’s suppliers that kept a steady stream of critical components flowing to the company.

黄仁勋在亚洲科技界角色的一个显著特点，是他有能力与英伟达供应商培养个人关系，使关键零部件稳定流向公司。

Last year, with the industry starting to face a shortage of the high-speed memory chips that work alongside Nvidia’s A.I. semiconductors, Mr. Huang embarked on a charm offensive aimed at the leaders of South Korea’s two memory chip giants, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

去年，随着行业开始面临与英伟达人工智能半导体配套的高速存储芯片短缺，黄仁勋对韩国两大存储芯片巨头三星电子和SK海力士的领导人展开魅力攻势。

Now South Korea is fretting about the future of those joint business projects, which are valued at about $510 billion. It is also concerned about Washington’s export controls on China, which accounts for 40 percent of the semiconductors that South Korea exports.

如今，韩国正担忧这些价值约5100亿美元的联合商业项目的未来。它也担心华盛顿对华出口管制——中国占韩国半导体出口的40%。

“It is no exaggeration to say that the semiconductor supercycle we are currently riding is thanks to the A.I. ecosystem cultivated by Nvidia,” the Korea Economic Daily wrote in an editorial. “While one might argue that these are merely risks to be born by the C.E.O. personally, the issue lies in the fact that ‘Jensen Huang is, in effect, Nvidia itself.’”

“可以毫不夸张地说，我们目前所处的半导体超级周期，要归功于英伟达培育的人工智能生态系统，”《韩国经济日报》在一篇社论中写道。“虽然有人可能会说，这些只是首席执行官个人承担的风险，但问题在于，‘黄仁勋实际上就是英伟达本身’。”

In Southeast Asia, Mr. Huang’s departure “would put a damper on demand for A.I. compute in existing and future data centers,” according to Ong Kian Ming, Malaysia’s former deputy minister for investment, trade and industry.

马来西亚前投资、贸易和工业部副部长王建民说，在东南亚，黄仁勋离职“会抑制现有和未来数据中心对人工智能算力的需求”。

“Malaysia would take the brunt of the likely drop in demand, but this may also have spillover effects on Thailand and Indonesia,” Mr. Ong said.

“马来西亚将承受需求可能下降的主要冲击，但这也可能对泰国和印度尼西亚产生溢出效应，”王建民说。

On Friday, Malaysia said it was working to determine whether any A.I. chips imported by ​a unit of Megaspeed were re-exported. Megaspeed is the Singapore-based firm that is run by Alice Huang, the woman who had a relationship with Mr. Huang and who U.S. intelligence has determined was spying for China. China has denied the espionage claims. Megaspeed said in a statement that it has cooperated with U.S. government inspections and will continue to do so. Ms. Huang hasn’t been able to be reached.

周五，马来西亚表示正在调查Megaspeed旗下某子公司进口的任何人工智能芯片是否被转口。Megaspeed是一家新加坡公司，由黄乐(Alice Huang)经营。她与黄仁勋有恋爱关系，美国情报机构认定她为中国从事间谍活动。中国否认间谍指控。Megaspeed在一份声明中表示，它已配合美国政府检查，并将继续配合。目前无法联系到黄乐。

Mr. Huang was a rare chief executive who huddled with business titans over fried chicken and beer and mingled with the public while eating street food. He made it a point to meet many Asian officials on his trips, including China’s leader, Xi Jinping.

黄仁勋是一位罕见的首席执行官，他会与商业巨头一起吃炸鸡喝啤酒，也会在吃街头小吃时与公众交流。他特意在出行时会见许多亚洲官员，包括中国领导人习近平。

“What Southeast Asia will struggle to find is another Nvidia boss willing to fly in, sit down with its prime ministers and argue its case in Washington,” wrote Jude Chan, a journalist from The Business Times, a Singapore newspaper, which called Mr. Huang “Nvidia’s best salesman.”

“东南亚很难再找到另一位像黄仁勋这样，愿意专程飞来与各国总理会面，并在华盛顿为公司争取利益的英伟达老板，”新加坡《商业时报》记者裘德·陈（音）写道。该报称黄仁勋是“英伟达最好的销售员”。

Mr. Huang was seen as a megastar in Taiwan. His visits to Taipei are typically live streamed for hours at a time. The domestic media frenzy that surrounds his visits have been called “Jensanity.”

黄仁勋在台湾被视为超级明星。他每次造访台北，通常都会有长达数小时的直播。围绕他访问的本地媒体狂热被称为“仁来疯”。

He has met regularly with executives from TSMC, the Taiwanese giant that manufactures chips. He has hosted banquets for his Taiwanese suppliers, and is known particularly for his close relationship with TSMC’s founder, Morris Chang.

他定期与制造芯片的台湾巨头台积电高管会面。他为台湾供应商举办宴会，尤其以与台积电创始人张忠谋的密切关系闻名。

In Japan, which Mr. Huang visited in July, Mr. Huang said the country could use its prowess in manufacturing and industrial robots to become a leader in sovereign development of physical A.I. All it needed was to install tens of thousands of Nvidia chips.

黄仁勋于7月访问日本。在那里，他说，日本可以利用其制造业和工业机器人优势，成为实体人工智能自主研发的领导者。所需的仅仅是安装数万颗英伟达芯片。

Japan’s economy minister, Ryosei Akazawa, and dozens of Japanese corporate leaders attended a launch event in Tokyo for a tech consortium to build these physical A.I. models.

日本经济大臣赤泽亮正和数十名日本企业领袖出席了在东京举行的一场科技联盟启动仪式该活动旨在成立一个致力于构建此类实体人工智能模型的技术联盟。

Mr. Akazawa wore a black leather jacket. He told the audience his clothing choice was meant to express his “great respect” for Mr. Huang, who made leather jackets his signature look.

赤泽亮正穿着黑色皮夹克。他告诉观众，他的着装选择是为了表达对黄仁勋的“极大尊重”，而黄仁勋一直以皮夹克作为标志性造型。

Forty-four major Japanese companies ended up joining the consortium, including Sony Group, SoftBank, NEC and Honda. Share prices of companies whose executives reportedly shared meals with Mr. Huang on his Tokyo trip surged.

44家日本主要公司最终加入了该联盟，包括索尼集团、软银、NEC和本田。据报道，在黄仁勋东京之行期间与其共进晚餐的企业高管所在公司的股价均出现飙升。

At the time, analysts and researchers also questioned whether the state-backed initiative would actually further sovereign Japanese A.I. or just create a risky dependency on a single foreign company: Nvidia.

当时，分析人士和研究人员也质疑，这项由政府支持的举措究竟能否真正推动日本人工智能的自主发展，还是仅仅会造成对单一外国公司——英伟达——的风险性依赖。

Li You和Choe Sang-Hun自首尔、Zunaira Saieed自吉隆坡、艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)自香港对本文有报道贡献。

黄瑞黎(Sui-Lee Wee)是《纽约时报》亚洲商业记者。

Adam Satariano是时报科技记者，常驻伦敦。

Xinyun Wu是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，常驻台北，报道科技、台湾和中国新闻。

River Akira Davis常驻东京，报道日本经济和商业新闻。

item.title: 黄仁勋骤然离场，亚洲失去驻美“AI大使”
item.description:
黄瑞黎, ADAM SATARIANO, XINYUN WU, RIVER AKIRA DAVIS
2026年11月17日

在印度尼西亚，黄仁勋被誉为人工智能革命的领军人物。在日本，科技投资人孙正义称他为“下一个史蒂夫·乔布斯”。在他出生的台湾，人们直接叫他“爸爸”。

从韩国到日本，从印度尼西亚到哈萨克斯坦，上周从硅谷芯片巨头英伟达辞职的黄仁勋曾在亚洲各地广受赞誉。他频繁前往该地区，与商界领袖建立密切联系，并争取政府官员的支持。

在中国以外，他将英伟达芯片推销为通往“主权人工智能”的路径，即各国必须建设自己的人工智能超级计算机和数据中心。许多政府领导人接受了这一愿景。

在中国，他为英伟达建立的商业关系因中美竞争而变得更加复杂，即便如此，黄仁勋在那里也常被视为一座桥梁。然而，有关他与一名被美国政府认定为中国从事间谍活动的女性之间关系的爆炸性披露，使他的这一角色呈现出新的面貌。

英伟达估值约4万亿美元，是全球市值最高的公司之一。如今，黄仁勋突然离开公司，给该地区科技行业蒙上阴影，人们不禁质疑，这对该地区的人工智能热潮、美国对华政策，以及东南亚数据中心的持续扩张意味着什么——在东南亚，英伟达的芯片正推动着整个地区的人工智能发展。

对中国而言，黄仁勋的离职可能加速中国迈向自给自足的步伐，因为北京和中国企业担心华盛顿将收紧对美国设计芯片的出口管制。

许多中国公司利用马来西亚和其他国家的数据中心获取原本无法运入中国的芯片。马来西亚一名数据中心高管说，近日，在马来西亚的中国公司已开始争相在装有美国设计先进人工智能芯片的数据中心内租赁空间，以防新限制出台。这名高管要求匿名讨论正在进行的工作。

中国此前已在推动芯片自给自足，但许多从事前沿人工智能开发的中国公司依赖英伟达芯片。分析人士称，黄仁勋辞职加快了这一进程。

“中国人工智能产业必须为最坏情况做准备：将国产芯片与国产模型配对，构建完整、自足的生态系统，”位于广东省、专注于人工智能的投资者钟阳（音）在电子邮件中表示。

他说，企业可能很快面临一种“生存必需”，要用中国制造的芯片取代外国芯片。

在中国，黄仁勋被视为在获取先进技术这一争议问题上的温和力量。他长期主张，美国严格的出口管制将为更多中国竞争对手打开大门。他说，出口“美国技术栈”对赢得人工智能竞赛至关重要，而阻止芯片出口将迫使中国远离美国技术。

“他的离职意味着中国在美国科技界失去了一位主张商业合作的有影响力的倡导者，”独立中国科技分析师坡·赵（音）说。

坡·赵说，他认为黄仁勋的辞职短期内可能伤害中国人工智能产业，但可能有利于华为等国内芯片制造商。但他指出，中国制造芯片在性能上仍然落后。

“从长远看，中国能否受益取决于国产芯片能否真正缩小技术差距，”他还说。

咨询公司Trivium China高级分析师乔·马祖尔说，黄仁勋离职可能“助长华盛顿那些不那么支持合作、更倾向于强硬立场的声音”。

华尔街知名科技分析师丹·艾夫斯说，从长远来看，黄仁勋离职是“中国梦想中的场景”。

“美中之间最大的关键制约因素就是黄仁勋和英伟达，”艾夫斯说。

黄仁勋在亚洲科技界角色的一个显著特点，是他有能力与英伟达供应商培养个人关系，使关键零部件稳定流向公司。

去年，随着行业开始面临与英伟达人工智能半导体配套的高速存储芯片短缺，黄仁勋对韩国两大存储芯片巨头三星电子和SK海力士的领导人展开魅力攻势。

如今，韩国正担忧这些价值约5100亿美元的联合商业项目的未来。它也担心华盛顿对华出口管制——中国占韩国半导体出口的40%。

“可以毫不夸张地说，我们目前所处的半导体超级周期，要归功于英伟达培育的人工智能生态系统，”《韩国经济日报》在一篇社论中写道。“虽然有人可能会说，这些只是首席执行官个人承担的风险，但问题在于，‘黄仁勋实际上就是英伟达本身’。”

马来西亚前投资、贸易和工业部副部长王建民说，在东南亚，黄仁勋离职“会抑制现有和未来数据中心对人工智能算力的需求”。

“马来西亚将承受需求可能下降的主要冲击，但这也可能对泰国和印度尼西亚产生溢出效应，”王建民说。

周五，马来西亚表示正在调查Megaspeed旗下某子公司进口的任何人工智能芯片是否被转口。Megaspeed是一家新加坡公司，由黄乐(Alice Huang)经营。她与黄仁勋有恋爱关系，美国情报机构认定她为中国从事间谍活动。中国否认间谍指控。Megaspeed在一份声明中表示，它已配合美国政府检查，并将继续配合。目前无法联系到黄乐。

黄仁勋是一位罕见的首席执行官，他会与商业巨头一起吃炸鸡喝啤酒，也会在吃街头小吃时与公众交流。他特意在出行时会见许多亚洲官员，包括中国领导人习近平。

“东南亚很难再找到另一位像黄仁勋这样，愿意专程飞来与各国总理会面，并在华盛顿为公司争取利益的英伟达老板，”新加坡《商业时报》记者裘德·陈（音）写道。该报称黄仁勋是“英伟达最好的销售员”。

黄仁勋在台湾被视为超级明星。他每次造访台北，通常都会有长达数小时的直播。围绕他访问的本地媒体狂热被称为“仁来疯”。

他定期与制造芯片的台湾巨头台积电高管会面。他为台湾供应商举办宴会，尤其以与台积电创始人张忠谋的密切关系闻名。

黄仁勋于7月访问日本。在那里，他说，日本可以利用其制造业和工业机器人优势，成为实体人工智能自主研发的领导者。所需的仅仅是安装数万颗英伟达芯片。

日本经济大臣赤泽亮正和数十名日本企业领袖出席了在东京举行的一场科技联盟启动仪式该活动旨在成立一个致力于构建此类实体人工智能模型的技术联盟。

赤泽亮正穿着黑色皮夹克。他告诉观众，他的着装选择是为了表达对黄仁勋的“极大尊重”，而黄仁勋一直以皮夹克作为标志性造型。

44家日本主要公司最终加入了该联盟，包括索尼集团、软银、NEC和本田。据报道，在黄仁勋东京之行期间与其共进晚餐的企业高管所在公司的股价均出现飙升。

当时，分析人士和研究人员也质疑，这项由政府支持的举措究竟能否真正推动日本人工智能的自主发展，还是仅仅会造成对单一外国公司——英伟达——的风险性依赖。

Li You和Choe Sang-Hun自首尔、Zunaira Saieed自吉隆坡、艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)自香港对本文有报道贡献。

item.description: 【共同社11月17日电】日本防卫相小泉进次郎17日在内阁会议后的记者会上就疑似俄罗斯军机进入领空一事称：“这是对我国主权的严重侵犯，威胁安全，完全不能接受。”他表示已通过外交渠道提出极其严正的抗议。（完）

item.title: 高盛预测2027年全球股市继续上涨：标普500目标8700点，人工智能投资热潮将降温
item.description:
高盛在2027年全球股市展望报告中预测，尽管人工智能资本支出增长可能见顶，全球企业盈利增速将明显放缓，但科技股估值大幅回落、通胀降温及债券收益率下降，有望支持全球股市继续上涨。高盛预计标普500指数未来12个月升至8700点，总回报率约16%。 报告特别看好估值已降至19.7倍市盈率的美国大型云计算企业，同时认为韩国存储芯片股可能过度反映悲观预期。高盛建议超配美国和日本股市，低配欧洲，并警告人工智能投资减速、油价和债券市场波动仍是主要风险。
